summary: Patterson sits on the flat western edge of the San Joaquin Valley, and the number that jumps off the page is its median home value of roughly $427,400 against a median household income near $93,500 — a price-to-income ratio around 4.6, which is genuinely attainable by Central Valley standards and almost unheard-of within a 90-minute drive of the Bay Area, where ratios routinely double that figure. That Bay Area proximity is the engine: Interstate 5 runs right through town, and the Diablo Range rises just to the west, making Patterson a textbook bedroom community where much of the workforce commutes north or west through Altamont Pass or over Pacheco Pass. The town itself covers under eight square miles, essentially a compact grid of newer subdivisions surrounded by almond orchards and irrigated farmland that stretches to the horizon in every direction — agriculture and food processing anchor the local job base, but switching employers without a long drive is difficult. Summers are searingly hot, with average highs well into the 90s and relentless sunshine averaging nearly ten hours a day, though winter nights dip into the low 40s and thick tule fog can blank out visibility for days. Median rent around $1,391 keeps housing costs moderate, and the poverty rate sits at a low 8.5%, but retail and dining options remain thin for a town of roughly 25,000 — most serious shopping or restaurant variety means a drive to Modesto or Turlock. Patterson delivers San Joaquin Valley affordability with a faint gravitational pull toward Silicon Valley, and the tradeoff is that nearly everything beyond your front door requires a car and, often, a lengthy commute.
